## Description

Freshwater heliozoan: a 40–50 µm sphere of foamy cytoplasm bristling with dozens of rigid axopodia
(microtubule bundles ~1 µm thick, one or two diameters long). It floats. Extrusomes on the axopodia
glue flagellates and ciliates that touch them; the axopodium shortens and brings the prey to the
body, which wraps it in a food vacuole.

## In the simulation

<!-- GENERATED:presence -->
Drops: `pond` (weight 0.15), `puddle` (weight 0.15); 2 individuals in a reference drop at weight 1.
<!-- /GENERATED -->

`feeding = "axopodia"`: anything within the axopodial reach (`tentacle_reach`) is captured and pulled
to the body, then engulfed with a phagocytic cup up to `mouth_width`. It does not swim
(`locomotion = "none"`). Axopodia are covering processes, drawn only.

## Literature

- Patterson D.J., Hausmann K. (1981) Eur. J. Cell Biol. 24: 67 (prey capture by the axopodia).
- Kreutz M., realmicrolife.com.
- Axopodial length and engulfable size are estimates; no published µmax (uses the general value).

## Not implemented yet

- Axopodia do not shorten individually or retract; they are not mechanical bodies.
- No fusion of several individuals to eat large prey (*Actinosphaerium*-like behaviour).
- Flotation is implicit (no vertical axis).

## Unique and shared mechanics

Its capture combines [`Captured`](../../mechanics/feeding-and-phagocytosis.md) (shared with suctorians) with the
[phagocytic cup](../../mechanics/feeding-and-phagocytosis.md) (shared with amoebae). The only heliozoan.
